q: A Raigarh steel plant runs its own coal mine: which scope do the mine's emissions go in?
title: Raigarh plant with its own mine: which scope
short: If your company owns or controls the mine, its diesel, explosives, electricity and mine methane are your own Scope 1 and 2, not Scope 3. Report the mine as a separate site so the plant figure and the mine figure can each be checked against their own records.
audience: Integrated steel and sponge iron groups in Raigarh with captive coal blocks

p: Under the GHG Protocol, emissions follow control. A captive block you operate is inside your boundary. Coal bought from a mine you do not operate is Scope 3, category 1.

ul: Diesel for haul trucks and shovels.
Grid or captive power for crushers and conveyors.

p: CBAM counts the steel plant's direct emissions and precursors, not mining. Your own inventory and lender reports should still include the mine, or they look smaller than they are.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer traces back to the documents behind it.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
